title: Build initial molecular structures
action: Generate initial Cartesian or Z‑matrix coordinates for all peroxyl radicals (CH₂ClO₂•, CHCl₂O₂•, CCl₃O₂•, CFCl₂O₂•, CF₂ClO₂•, CHFClO₂•), parent halomethanes, alkyl radicals, anions, and small fragments (H, O₂).
description: Create initial geometries for all species needed in subsequent calculations.

title: Geometry optimization and frequency calculations
action: Perform full geometry optimizations and vibrational frequency calculations at MP2(full)/6‑31G(d,p) and B3LYP/6‑31G(d,p) for all species required for later thermochemistry and property analysis. Save optimized geometries and wavefunction data.
description: The core computational stage that determines equilibrium structures, zero‑point energies, and thermal corrections.

title: Extract structural parameters
action: From the optimized geometries, extract the C‑O and O‑O bond lengths, the C‑O‑O bond angle, and the X‑C‑O‑O torsion angles for each peroxyl radical at both MP2 and B3LYP levels and write the results to geometries.csv.
description: Structural parameters as in Table I: distances in Å, angles in degrees.
output_schema: Columns: Radical (string), Method (string), R_C1O2 (float, Å), R_O2O3 (float, Å), Angle_C1O2O3 (float, degrees), Torsion_X4 (float, degrees), Torsion_X5 (float, degrees), Torsion_X6 (float, degrees). One row per radical‑method combination.

title: Compute charge, spin density, and dipole moment
action: Perform Mulliken population analysis on the MP2 and B3LYP wavefunctions to obtain atomic charges and spin densities for C1, O2, O3, and compute dipole moments. Write the data to charge_spin_dipole.json.
description: Charge distributions, spin densities, and dipole moments as in Table II.
output_schema: Array of objects; each object has properties: radical (string), method (string, 'MP2' or 'B3LYP'), dipole_moment (float, Debye), atoms (array of objects with symbol (string), charge (float), spin_density (float)). Atom order: C1, O2, O3.

title: Higher‑level single‑point energy calculations
action: Compute single‑point energies at MP4(SDTQ)/6‑311+G(d,p) and B3LYP/6‑311+G(2df,2p) using the optimized geometries from step 2 for all species involved in thermochemistry.
description: Refined energies needed for the isodesmic BDE estimation.

title: Compute C‑H bond dissociation energies
action: Calculate C‑H BDEs for parent halomethanes using isodesmic reactions and the experimental BDE(CH₄)=104.9 kcal/mol; combine with ZPE and thermal corrections from step 2. Write results to CH_BDEs.csv.
description: C‑H bond dissociation energies for parent methanes at MP2/6‑31G(d,p) and B3LYP/6‑31G(d,p) levels.
output_schema: Columns: Level (string, e.g., B3LYP/6‑31G(d,p)), CH4 (float, kcal/mol), CH3Cl (float), CH2Cl2 (float), CHCl3 (float), CHFCl2 (float), CHF2Cl (float), CH2FCl (float).

title: Compute C‑O bond dissociation energies
action: Calculate C‑O BDEs for the peroxyl radicals via isodesmic reactions, using the experimental BDE(CH₃‑O₂)=32.7 kcal/mol and energies/ZPE from steps 2 and 5. Write results to CO_BDEs.csv.
description: C‑O bond dissociation energies for the studied peroxyl radicals at MP2/6‑31G(d,p) and B3LYP/6‑31G(d,p) levels.
output_schema: Columns: Level (string), CH3‑O2 (float, kcal/mol), CH2Cl‑O2 (float), CHCl2‑O2 (float), CCl3‑O2 (float), CFCl2‑O2 (float), CF2Cl‑O2 (float), CHFCl‑O2 (float).

title: Single‑point calculations with diffuse basis for electron affinity
action: Run single‑point energy calculations at MP2/6‑31+G(d,p) and B3LYP/6‑31+G(d,p) for the peroxyl radicals and their corresponding anions using the optimized geometries from step 2.
description: Energies needed for electron affinity calculation.

title: Compute electron affinities
action: Calculate adiabatic electron affinities as the difference between the total electronic energies of the radical and the anion species obtained in step 8. Write results to EAs.csv.
description: Electron affinities of the peroxyl radicals at MP2/6‑31+G(d,p) and B3LYP/6‑31+G(d,p).
output_schema: Columns: Level (string), CH3‑O2 (float, kcal/mol), CH2Cl‑O2 (float), CHCl2‑O2 (float), CCl3‑O2 (float), CFCl2‑O2 (float), CF2Cl‑O2 (float), CHFCl‑O2 (float).
